- Origin story: Radico's Shaw Wallace bottling contract expired in the mid-1990s. Lalit Khaitan approached United Spirits for a partnership and was refused, which he believed was because Vijay Mallya wanted a stake in Radico. Radico then launched its own brands. **8PM whisky launched 8 Aug 1998** — [StockEdge](https://blog.stockedge.com/stock-insights-radico-khaitan-ltd/). So the real "UB" link is the 1990s Mallya rebuff, which pushed Radico to build brands of its own.

`case_study:theranos-2015` | 2015-10-15 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Private blood-testing startup Theranos was valued at ~$9 bn (2014) on claims that a finger-prick device could run hundreds of tests. In Oct 2015 John Carreyrou (WSJ) revealed it ran most tests on modified commercial analysers and that its own device was unreliable; regulators sanctioned its lab; the company dissolved in 2018. Elizabeth Holmes was convicted on four fraud counts and sentenced to 11.25 years (Nov 2022). Visible flags: (1) no peer-reviewed data or independent validation; (2) a board of statesmen/generals rather than lab scientists; (3) extreme secrecy and NDAs, employee turnover; (4) investors (family offices, media owners) without healthcare diligence; Walgreens' partnership skipped proper testing; (5) founder charisma substituted for evidence. Lesson for listed markets: deep-tech/biotech claims need third-party validation (peer review, regulatory approvals, customer audits); a 'celebrity' board is a governance red flag, not comfort. Included briefly as a private-market case; no listed tickers.

**Lesson:** Demand independent validation of technical claims
**Spotted early by:** John Carreyrou (WSJ); whistleblowers Tyler Shultz, Erika Cheung

`strategy:marks-cycle-temperature` | confidence: **single-source** | tags: global, india, process, base-rate, avoid-ruin

You can't predict, but you can prepare: estimate where the market is in its cycle and adjust aggression gradually. Marks's 'temperature' inputs: investor psychology (greed vs fear), credit availability and lending standards, issuance quality (IPOs of loss-making or tiny firms), valuation vs history, and the prevailing narrative ('this time is different'). Indian temperature checklist: smallcap/midcap P/E premium to Nifty; mainboard and SME IPO counts and subscription multiples; retail F&O volumes and new demat additions; market cap/GDP (above ~120% = hot, below ~70% = cold, per 2008/2020/2024 history); NBFC/corporate bond spreads; FPI positioning and the rupee. Posture rule: in hot readings, raise quality, trim small caps, keep dry powder; in cold readings, deploy in steps. Second-level thinking: ask what consensus expects and what is priced, not just whether a company is good. Limitation: temperature readings are early by months or years.

Links: person:howard-marks (about); insight:india-cycle-top-bottom-signals (about)

Sources: <https://www.privatedebtinvestor.com/oaktree-raises-10-9bn-distressed-fund/>

`case_study:titan-2009-2026` · tickers: TITAN · confidence: single-source

Split-adjusted ₹36 (Mar 2009) → ₹4,700 on 19 Nov 2026 ≈130x (ATH ₹5,169, Aug 2026). Twin engine: P/E 20.8 → 58.7 (2.8x) × implied EPS ~46x; about 21% of the log-return was rerating, among the most earnings-driven cases here. Drawdowns: −57% (2007–09), then ≤−38% (2019–20 COVID), with several −30% dips (2011, 2012–13, 2015–16). Sales ₹11.9k cr (FY15) → ₹87.6k cr (FY26). Early signal (general knowledge, unverified narrative): Tanishq taking share from unorganised jewellers on trust and purity (karat-meter, exchange programmes), later helped by mandatory hallmarking (2021); Tata parentage; store additions disclosed quarterly. The 2009 entry at ~21x was the cheap window. Rakesh Jhunjhunwala's large holding is the famous example (see existing records; the '₹3' entry is a separate myth record). Not ended: EPS jumped FY26 (₹57 → ₹79 TTM) while P/E compressed from 90–190 (2020–24) to ~59. Lesson: formalisation of a huge unorganised category is a multi-decade earnings engine; buying at 60–100x worked only because EPS kept compounding at 20%+.

Key data: **start_year**: 2009; **end_year**: 2026; **start_price**: 36; **end_price**: 4700; **multiple**: ~130x; **pe_start**: 20.8; **pe_end**: 58.7; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~46x; **max_drawdown**: -38% (2019-20); **early_signals**: unorganised→organised share gain; trust brand; **ended**: still running; **lesson**: formalisation themes = long EPS runways

`case_study:kpit-technologies-2020-2024` · tickers: KPITTECH · confidence: verified

Relisted Apr 2019 after the Birlasoft demerger. ₹44 (Mar 2020) → ATH ₹1,866 (Jul 2024) ≈42x; P/E 8.5 → 86 (10x) × implied EPS ~4.1x. About 62% of the log-return was rerating, the second-highest share in this library. Drawdowns inside: −34% (2022). After: −74% to ₹479 (Oct 2026); ₹522 on 19 Nov 2026 while TTM EPS is flat (₹21.6 → ₹21.0) and P/E is ~25. Early signal: a pure-play automotive software firm (AUTOSAR, EV powertrain, ADAS middleware) at a COVID P/E of 8.5; revenue growth of 20%+ with OPM rising from 14% to 21%, and deal wins with global OEMs announced through 2020–23. Ended: FY26 PAT ₹637 cr vs ₹840 cr in FY25. On 1 Jul 2026 a profit warning said Q1 FY27 revenue would decline for the first time in 23 quarters as European OEMs (BMW, VW) cut spending; there is high BMW concentration. The stock fell ~16% that day, JPMorgan downgraded to Underweight and the stock was ~−52% YTD. Lesson: a thematic multibagger made mostly of multiple expansion, with revenue concentrated in a few European car makers, has no earnings cushion when the theme's customers retrench.

Key data: **start_year**: 2020; **end_year**: 2024; **start_price**: 44.3; **end_price**: 1866; **price_nov2026**: 522; **multiple**: ~42x; **pe_start**: 8.5; **pe_end**: 86.4; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~4.1x; **max_drawdown**: -34% in run; -74% after; **early_signals**: pure-play auto software at 8.5x; margin expansion; **ended**: Jul 2026 profit warning; Europe OEM cuts; BMW concentration; **lesson**: rerating-heavy + client concentration = round trip

`case_study:la-opala-2009-2015` · tickers: LAOPALA · confidence: verified

Split/bonus-adjusted ₹1.55 (Mar 2009) → ₹306 (Dec 2015) ≈198x; P/E 17.5 → 70 (4x) × implied EPS ~50x (from a depressed FY09 base). The run had shallow drawdowns (−32%). Early signal: the Diva opal-glass dinnerware brand (launched 2009) reached ~50% of revenue by 2014 with price increases; Sitarganj plant capacity of 8,000 tpa ran at ~85% utilisation and was doubled in late 2015; OPM 30–42%. Investors such as Ashish Kacholia held it. Ended: the stock went nowhere. ₹306 (Dec 2015) → ₹161 on 19 Nov 2026 (−48%; −70% from the 2023 ATH ₹468). Standalone sales ₹222 cr (FY15) → ₹309 cr (FY26), about 3% CAGR; EPS ~₹8. A greenfield expansion (FY22) arrived ahead of demand, with competition from Borosil and imports (narrative partly unverified). Lesson: high margins and ROCE do not equal runway. Opalware dinnerware is a small total addressable market. The rerating to 70x priced a long runway that did not exist, so check category size before extrapolating early growth.

Key data: **start_year**: 2009; **end_year**: 2015; **start_price**: 1.55; **end_price**: 306; **price_nov2026**: 161; **multiple**: ~198x; **pe_start**: 17.5; **pe_end**: 69.6; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~50x; **max_drawdown**: -32% in run; -70% from 2023 ATH; **early_signals**: Diva brand 50% of sales; capacity at 85% utilisation; **ended**: small TAM; ~3% sales CAGR FY15-26; **lesson**: check TAM before paying for runway

`insight:india-rates-rupee-regime-2025-26` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-06-05

RBI cut the repo rate through 2025 (from 6.50% in early 2025 to 5.25% by Dec-2025 per subsequent reports) and on 5 Jun 2026 held at 5.25% with a neutral stance, choosing FX-inflow measures over hikes after the war-driven crude spike; it cut its FY27 GDP forecast to 6.6% and raised CPI to 5.1%. The rupee went from ~Rs83/$ in early FY25 and ~Rs90 in 2025 to a record closing low of ~96.86 on 20 May 2026 (reports cite 'near Rs97'). Mechanics for an equity investor: (1) FPI outflows, a wider current-account deficit (oil) and a weaker rupee reinforce each other; in USD terms the Nifty's 2026 drawdown was materially worse than in INR; (2) rate cuts help rate-sensitive sectors (NBFCs, real estate, autos) with a 2-4 quarter lag, but rupee stress can cap further easing; (3) a falling rupee helps IT services, pharma exporters and specialty chemicals with USD revenue and hurts oil marketers, importers and companies with unhedged foreign-currency debt; (4) long-run: INR has depreciated roughly 3-4% a year vs USD over decades, so Indian equity returns must be compared with US returns after FX. Base rate: crude oil shocks (2008, 2013 taper + CAD, 2022, 2026) are the recurring trigger for Indian macro stress. Actionable: check each holding's FX exposure (USD revenue share, foreign-currency borrowings, import content) and include an oil/rupee stress case in valuations.

Sources:
- https://theprint.in/economy/rbi-pauses-rate-cuts-retains-interest-rate-at-5-25-pc/2847398
- https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/indian-economy-remains-resilient-rbi-governor-malhotra
- https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/rbi-holds-interest-rates-as-oil-shock-clouds-outlook-unveils-measures-to-support-rupee
- https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/rbi-june-2026-mpc-policy-analysis-rupee

1. **For a bank, the "good" numbers mislead more than the bad ones** (10 good-but-misleading rows vs 6 bad-but-benign).
   The disciplined move is re-deriving growth ex the special window and GNPA ex write-offs.
2. **The cost of equity decides everything again.** At 12.5% the price needs ~22% ROE; the market's implied CoE is ~7%.
   Report implied CoE and the own-history P/B band; treat "RIM value" as a hurdle check (L21 generalises to P/B).
3. **Dilution must be in the denominator before any P/B.** Warrants at ₹227 cut ROE on book by ~1.5–2 pp until deployed.
4. **Credibility needs a sector-adjusted, bias-aware score.** Conservative guidance → A grade; meaningless without peers.
5. **Depth lived in the boring notes again (L13):** Schedule 16 (DICGC, card-network, outsourcing), the PSL-shortfall
   line, the divergence note, the fraud note and the AS-18 table were not mentioned by any analyst on six calls.

- **S1 negative equity (adjusted):** E < 0, **unless** buyback-driven and cash-generative: FCF(FY0) > 0 **and**
  TreasuryStockValue(FY0) + Σ(D + B) over the last 3 fiscal years filed ≤ T ≥ |E|. Exempted firms are not fired.
  Reported alongside: **S1raw** = any E < 0 (secondary).
- **S2 interest cover:** I > 0 and EBIT / I < 1.5 (negative EBIT with any interest fires). I missing or 0 ⇒
  not fired if TD < 5% of total assets, else unknown.
- **S3 short-term funding gap:** STD > 0 and STD > C + 0.5 × CFO (CFO with its sign: cash burners get no credit).
- **S4 payouts beyond FCF while borrowing:** D + B > 0 and D + B > FCF and TD(FY0) > TD(FY−1).
- **S5 combined:** ≥ 2 of S1–S4 fired (unknown counts as not fired; S5 known if ≥ 2 component flags known).
- Reference only (not a candidate): **S0** EBIT < 0 (operating loss) — tells us whether S2's lift is just "loss-maker".

body:
| Item | Pre-registered choice |
|---|---|
| Universe | US operating companies filing a 10-K (not 10-K/A) in calendar 2021, 2022 or 2023 that also filed a 10-K 9–15 months earlier. Public float (dei `EntityPublicFloat`, cover page of the same 10-K) **$300M–$10B**. Excluded: SIC 6000–6799 (banks, insurers, brokers, REITs, SPACs, funds), 4900–4999 (utilities), blank SIC. |
| Sample | If the full universe is too heavy: a seeded random sample of firms (seed 20261122) from the frame-based candidate list, taken in shuffled order until ≥ 800 eligible firm-years per filing year; the draw order and every exclusion are logged. |
| Text | 10-K primary document only (no exhibits). HTML/iXBRL tags stripped (hidden `ix:header` removed), entities unescaped, lower-cased, tokens = alphabetic words ≥ 2 letters; numbers dropped. |
| Sections | (a) full text; (b) Item 1A Risk Factors; (c) Item 7 MD&A — extracted as the longest span between a section heading and the next item heading (skips the table of contents). A section shorter than 1,500 characters in either year → missing for that measure. |
| Similarity | **Cosine similarity of raw term-frequency vectors** (this year vs prior year). Secondary: Jaccard similarity of word sets. |
| Signal | Within each filing year, quintiles of similarity. **"Changers" = bottom quintile (least similar), "non-changers" = top quintile.** |
| Entry | Adjusted close on the first trading day **after** the 10-K filing date (EDGAR acceptance date). |
| Horizons | 3, 6, 12 months = 63, 126, 252 trading days. |
| **Primary metric** | **Full-text cosine, changers minus size-matched controls, 12-month return.** Expected sign: negative. |
| Controls | For each event, 5 random (seeded) firm-years from the same filing year's sample, **not** in the event's own quintile group, market cap at entry within ×0.6–×1.67, with price data over the same calendar window (return measured from the event's entry date). |
| Secondary | Same at 3/6 m; non-changers vs controls; changers − non-changers spread; Item 1A and Item 7 cosine; Jaccard (full); per filing year. Six-plus secondary tests → treat any lone secondary "hit" as a hypothesis only. |
| Stats | Mean, median, 1/99% winsorised mean, hit rate, naive t; **95% bootstrap CI resampling filing months** (2,000 draws). |
| Costs | 0.5% round-trip. For the avoid use, the benefit of skipping a changer = −(excess return); cost-adjusted benefit = −excess − 0.5%. |
| **Decision rule** | Call it an edge only if the primary metric has **t ≤ −3, or its 95% month-bootstrap CI lies entirely below −0.5%** (i.e. excludes zero after costs). Otherwise "not proven" (if negative) or "rejected" (if ≥ 0 with CI excluding the paper-sized effect). |
| Survivorship | Firms with no Yahoo series or series ending inside the window are audited via EDGAR submissions: 8-K item 1.03 (bankruptcy), merger forms (DEFM14A / SC TO-T / SC 14D9 / 25-NSE / Form 15). Report counts by quintile and a bound. |
| Use if it works | Long-only: an **avoid / look-harder list** (bottom-quintile changers for 12 months after the 10-K). Shorting is out of scope. |
